## Recall · Lecture 9

a) What does the app review check a game against?
b) The listing shows screenshots of another game. What will the review say?
c) Which step comes right before the release?

::: {.answer}
a) the store's guidelines
b) It is a misleading listing.
c) the review
:::

## Activity 1 · The five parts · 10 min

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- The guidelines have five parts: Safety, Performance, Business, Design and Legal.
- The rules change often, so we read the official page and its date.
- **Do it:** Find the part about in-app purchases on the official page, then sort the nine problems in Guideline Sorter.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/guideline-parts.png)
:::
::::

## Live demo · Guideline Sorter

{{< sim file="sims/guideline-sorter.html" poster="sims/guideline-sorter.png" title="Guideline Sorter: which part of the rules?" task="**Show:** sort a chat for children, a paid mystery chest and a crash on start. **Ask:** which part of the guidelines does each one belong to?" >}}

## Check 1 · The five parts

What does a good answer show?

::: {.reveal}
1. It names the official page and its date, for example Apple's App Review Guidelines.
2. It finds purchases in part 3, Business, under 3.1 In-App Purchase.
3. Chat goes to Safety, crashes to Performance, purchases to Business, copies to Design, and privacy to Legal.
:::

## Activity 2 · Why rejected? · 10 min

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A rejection names the rule that the game broke.
- Gem Rush hides the odds of a paid mystery chest, so it breaks a Business rule.
- **Do it:** For two games you know, write one rule that each must follow, and its part.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/rejection-reasons.png)
:::
::::

## Check 2 · Why rejected?

What does a good answer show?

::: {.reveal}
1. A football game sells coins, so it follows a Business rule: the store's own payment.
2. A puzzle game has a chat, so it follows a Safety rule: report and block.
3. Each rule fits something the game really has.
:::

## Activity 3 · A checklist · 12 min

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A checklist turns the guidelines into yes-or-no questions.
- A game with chat needs reporting and blocking, and a game with purchases needs store payments.
- **Do it:** Write eight yes-or-no lines for a game you know, each with its part.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/checklist.png)
:::
::::

## Check 3 · A checklist

What does a good checklist for a game with purchases and chat contain?

::: {.reveal}
1. It asks about crashes, "coming soon" buttons and real screenshots for Performance.
2. It asks about the privacy policy and licences for Legal, and store purchases and odds for Business.
3. It asks about report and block in the chat for Safety.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/review-board.html" poster="sims/review-board.png" title="Review Board: approve or reject?" kind="game" task="**The story:** today you are the reviewer, and six games wait for a decision. **Play:** approve or reject each game, with the right reason, on your phone." >}}

## Try it · Review Board (harder)

The facts: Tiny Chat Pets lets children chat with strangers without a filter. Gem Rush hides the odds of its paid mystery chest. Hero Wars X uses the heroes of a famous film without a licence.

a) Which part of the guidelines rejects Tiny Chat Pets?
b) What must Gem Rush change before it can pass?
c) Which part of the guidelines rejects Hero Wars X?

::: {.answer}
a) Safety
b) It must show the odds before the purchase.
c) Legal, because of the intellectual property of others
:::

## Wrap-up

- You can find the main parts of the official guidelines and their date.
- You can say why a game is rejected, with the part and the rule.
- You can build a pre-submission checklist that fits a game.
